text: Differences in the hypertrophic potential between trained and untrained people can be attributed to the ceiling effect, or window of adaptation (). During the initial stages of training, the neuromuscular system is deconditioned and responds to virtually any stimulus because the ceiling for growth is high. Even steady-state cardiorespiratory exercise has been shown to produce hypertrophic increases in previously sedentary individuals (41). As people become resistance trained and move closer to their genetic ceiling, however, it becomes progressively more difficult to increase muscular size (i.e., the window of adaptation becomes smaller).
